canvas-01.description: The lower half of sheet 1, below the key map, is a street map at 100 feet to an inch of the north-western edge of Allendale along West Maple Avenue and Hillside Avenue, which run parallel across the sheet. Thomas Avenue joins them at the west, Lake runs between them in the middle, and West Crescent Avenue runs along the east edge, with West Allendale Avenue meeting it in the north-east corner beside Ramsey Brook. The two blocks between West Maple and Hillside Avenues (blocks 32 and 33) are divided into narrow house lots, built up mostly with one- and two-storey frame dwellings and auto houses, more densely east of Lake. North of West Maple Avenue and south of Hillside Avenue the land is in large lots with scattered dwellings. West of Thomas Avenue, where the streets end, are a greenhouse on a brick base, two water towers, a dwelling with a stone first storey and other dwellings and outbuildings on large tracts (blocks 2, 3 and 31). A 6-inch water pipe from Ramsey runs along Hillside Avenue. The top half of the same page carries the key map of the borough at 1000 feet to an inch, the index of specials, the water and fire department report and a location map of New Jersey; those are not part of this map.
notes: The page is labelled Index in the scan; its upper half is the key map at 1000 feet to an inch and was not georeferenced.
Lake (printed without a suffix) is Lake Street in OpenStreetMap.
A 6-inch water pipe from Ramsey is marked along Hillside Avenue.

map. Sheet 1 (labelled Index in the scan). Upper half: key map at 1000 ft to an inch, index of specials, water and fire report (not georeferenced). Lower half: street map at 100 ft to an inch of West Maple Av, Hillside Av, Thomas Av, Lake and West Crescent Av; configured as one part (canvas-01) masked below the dividing double line.

sheet-2.description: Sheet 2 covers the western and central part of Allendale at 100 feet to an inch, from West Crescent Avenue on the west to Maple Street on the east and from beyond Myrtle Avenue on the north to Brookside Avenue on the south. The double-track Erie Railroad main line crosses the sheet diagonally from north-west to south-east, and the North Jersey Rapid Transit Co. (electric) right of way runs parallel to it further north before curving south. North of the railroad, Myrtle Avenue is lined with narrow numbered house lots, mostly with frame dwellings, and A. Court (marked arbitrary) runs north from Myrtle Avenue. The business centre lies where West Allendale Avenue and Park Avenue meet the railroad: a row of stores, a drug store and an auto repair shop on the north side of the tracks, the post office on Maple Street, and on the south side the depot, a train shed, a hotel and the public library. South of the tracks are the Municipal Building with the fire department on Park Avenue, and the yard of the Allendale Coal and Lumber Co. with lumber sheds, sash and door warehouses, coal pockets and a siding. Mallinson Avenue and Park Avenue run south to Brookside Avenue through blocks of dwellings; West Orchard Street and Dale Avenue appear at the south-east corner. The west half of the sheet is mostly open land: an athletic field with a grand stand between West Allendale Avenue and Hillside Avenue, crossed by Ramsey Brook. Elm Street and Maple Street appear in the north-east, and a corner of Franklin Turnpike is drawn at the top right.
notes: Mallinson Avenue is Mallinson Street in OpenStreetMap; the unnamed street between blocks 54 and 22 east of Mallinson is 1st Street today.
The Erie Railroad (E.R.R.) main line and depot, and the North Jersey Rapid Transit Co. (electric) right of way, cross the sheet; the trolley line has since been abandoned.
Municipal Building and fire department on Park Avenue; public library and hotel by the depot; Allendale Coal and Lumber Co. yard south of the tracks.
Junctions on West Crescent Avenue fit 5 to 7 m worse than those in the eastern half of the sheet.
map. Scale 100 ft. West Crescent Av to Maple St, Myrtle Av to Brookside Av: business centre at the Erie depot, Municipal Building, Allendale Coal & Lumber Co., athletic field. One part.

sheet-3.description: Sheet 3 covers the eastern part of central Allendale at 100 feet to an inch, centred on Franklin Turnpike, which crosses the sheet from north-west to south-east. Maple Street runs along the west edge, with Elm Street and West Allendale Avenue leading from it to the turnpike; East Allendale Avenue runs north-north-east from the turnpike to the top of the sheet, with Cottage Place and Powell Heights branching from it, and West and East Orchard Street cross the turnpike near the bottom. The blocks between Maple Street and the turnpike are lined with frame dwellings and hold the Chapel of the Guardian Angel R.C. Church at Maple and Elm. Along the turnpike stand the Archer Memorial M.E. Church with its Sunday school, a public garage for 30 cars, the Allendale Public School and the Episcopal church near East Orchard Street. North of Cottage Place are greenhouses on concrete bases and a private pump station on a ditch, described as draining a large swamp, with electric turbine pumps. A brook runs south from Elm Street past the turnpike, widening into a pond near West Orchard Street. Much of the area east of East Allendale Avenue and south of Powell Heights is large undivided lots with scattered dwellings and outbuildings. In the south-west corner the Erie Railroad main line and the North Jersey Rapid Transit Co. (electric) right of way cross the sheet, with Dale Avenue at the bottom left edge.
notes: Powell Heights is Powell Road in OpenStreetMap.
Franklin Turnpike meets West Allendale Avenue and East Allendale Avenue at two junctions about 20 m apart on the sheet; today they form one junction, which was not used as control.
Archer Memorial M.E. Church, Allendale Public School, Episcopal church and the Chapel of the Guardian Angel R.C. Church are drawn on this sheet.
A private pump station for draining a large swamp stands on a ditch north of Cottage Place.
map. Scale 100 ft. Franklin Turnpike between Maple St and East Allendale Av, Cottage Pl, Powell Heights (Powell Road), East and West Orchard St; schools and churches. One part.

sheet-4-1.description: The east part of sheet 4, right of the heavy dividing line, covers southern Allendale at 100 feet to an inch from West Orchard Street and Brookside Avenue at the top to West Crescent Avenue at the bottom. Mallinson Avenue and Park Avenue run south from Brookside Avenue and join just north of New Street; Park Avenue then continues south-west across Ramsey Brook and Hohokus Brook to meet West Crescent Avenue at the bottom of the sheet. Between Mallinson and Park Avenues are 3rd and 4th Streets with small blocks of house lots (blocks 24 and 25), and north of 3rd Street a park (block 23) fronts Brookside Avenue. East of Park Avenue a long row of narrow lots (block 26) runs down to New Street, with Dale Avenue parallel further east and a further strip of lots beyond it (block 29). New Street runs east from Park Avenue to Dale Avenue with a row of dwellings on its south side. The buildings are almost all frame dwellings and auto houses; an auto painting shop stands on Park Avenue. South of New Street the land is open, crossed by Ramsey Brook and Hohokus Brook, which meet the dividing line on the west. Water pipes and hydrants are marked along Brookside, Park and West Crescent Avenues.
notes: Mallinson Avenue is Mallinson Street in OpenStreetMap; 4th Street is not in the OpenStreetMap extract.
New Street / Park Avenue was left out of the fit: it fitted 5 to 7 m worse than the other points, which suggests the modern junction has moved.
Dale Avenue / New Street was not used: the drawn T junction lies about 8 m from the modern junction.

map. Scale 100 ft. Two parts divided by a heavy vertical line: part 1 (east) Brookside Av, Mallinson Av, Park Av, Dale Av, New St down to West Crescent Av; part 2 (west) Franklin Turnpike, West/East Crescent Av, Heights Rd, Crescent Pl, Woodland Av, Ivers Rd. Part 2 has control only along West Crescent Av (helmert).

sheet-4-2.description: The west part of sheet 4, left of the heavy dividing line, covers the northern edge of Allendale at 100 feet to an inch along West Crescent Avenue, which runs down the sheet. At the top Franklin Turnpike crosses diagonally and meets West Crescent Avenue, which continues north as East Crescent Avenue. Further south Heights Road, Crescent Place and Woodland Avenue run west from West Crescent Avenue, and Ivers Road leaves it eastward at the bottom. Heights Road is lined on both sides by a regular row of narrow numbered lots (block 50, 4A), only some of them built on; Crescent Place and Woodland Avenue have a few dwellings each. The North Jersey Rapid Transit Co. (electric) right of way crosses the lower half diagonally from north-west to south-east, cutting across Woodland Avenue. The remaining land, west of the turnpike and around the right of way, is in large lots with scattered frame dwellings and outbuildings. An 8-inch water pipe from Ramsey runs along Franklin Turnpike, and water pipes and hydrants are marked along West Crescent Avenue and Heights Road.
notes: The North Jersey Rapid Transit Co. (electric) right of way crosses Woodland Avenue; the line has since been abandoned.
All usable control lies along West Crescent Avenue, so the part is placed with a helmert transformation (position, scale and rotation only).
